run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T14:40:30Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by frontend's own error spans on two dependency paths: calls to ad (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, which drive GET /api/data) and calls made by checkout to payment (grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, which drive POST /api/checkout). Errors began at ~14:40:30, exactly when the alert fired, and cleared by ~14:53. At 14:39:26-14:39:30 the ad and payment Deployments in otel-demo were both replaced by new ReplicaSets whose pod templates are identical to their predecessors except for the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt (a rollout restart; same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad / :2.1.3-payment, same env, same resource limits). Neither Deployment has a readiness or liveness probe and each Service has a single backend pod, so the replacement pod entered the Service endpoints while its process was not yet listening: the new ad pod logged "Ad service starting." at 14:44:09.9 and "Ad service started, listening on 8080" at 14:45:49.9 (container started 14:39:29), and ad served zero GetAds server spans in the windows ending 14:45:16, 14:47:16 and 14:49:16, while frontend's GetAds spans were 100% error. The new payment pod logged "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" only at 14:40:51.5 (container started 14:39:29), which matches the checkout->PaymentService/Charge error burst at 14:40-14:43. The ad rollout gap is the dominant contributor to the frontend alert (417 error GetAds spans and the same count on GET /api/data in 14:40-14:59, versus 76 on the checkout path). No pod crash, OOM, eviction, image change, node pressure or config change was found; the failure is a startup-availability gap exposed by the rollout restart, made visible because the workloads have no readiness gates.

claims.text: frontend recorded 1963.18 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans versus 94364.97 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans over 2026-11-16T13:40:30Z-14:59:16Z in traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend"}, i.e. the alerting service itself has error spans in this window.

frontend's error spans are confined to nine span_names: grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds 407.68, GET /api/data 407.68, executing api route (pages) /api/data 407.68, GET 407.68, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 79.3, POST /api/checkout 79.3, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 79.3, POST 79.3 and tcp.connect 15.25 (increase over the whole window); no error spans were recorded on grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct or grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations.

Error spans by service over the window: frontend 1963.18, frontend-proxy 1006.5 (operations "ingress" 519.52 and "router frontend egress" 486.98), checkout 152 (oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 76 and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 76), recommendation 4.07, ad 2.35, fraud-detection 1.02, accounting 0 and payment 0.

Frontend error spans appeared only at the alert time: in 300s windows stepping through the incident, GET /api/data (and its GetAds child) had 0 errors at the 14:20:30-14:35:30 points, 4.21 at 14:40:30, 280 at 14:45:30, 417.89 at 14:50:30 and 150.35 at 14:55:30; POST /api/checkout had 6.32 at 14:40:30, 82.11 at 14:45:30, 75.79 at 14:50:30 and 0 at 14:55:30.

Frontend's GetAds client spans failed almost completely during the incident: 0 error / 294.44 unset in the 300s window ending 14:39:16, then 166.67 error / 113.33 unset (ending 14:43:16), 291.11 error / 0 unset (14:45:16), 295.56 error / 0 unset (14:47:16), 238.75 error / 25 unset (14:49:16), 105.78 error / 161.71 unset (14:51:16) and 0 error / 176.18 unset (14:53:16) - i.e. a total ad-path outage followed by recovery.

The ad service itself served nothing during that period: its own server-span series for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds shows 295.56 spans in the 300s window ending 14:39:16, 263.75 (14:41:16), 107.78 (14:43:16), then exactly 0 (14:45:16), 0 (14:47:16), 0 (14:49:16), recovering to 149.33 (14:51:16) and 159 (14:53:16).

Kubernetes events show a rollover of both workloads at the alert onset: for ad, SuccessfulCreate of ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 (14:39:27), Scheduled 14:39:27, Created/Started container ad 14:39:29, and Killing + SuccessfulDelete of the old pod ad-554b849958-6z62j by ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 at 14:39:29; for payment, SuccessfulCreate of payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn (14:39:26), Created/Started container payment 14:39:29-14:39:30, and Killing + SuccessfulDelete of old pod payment-55766d76b9-9fxhp at 14:39:30. All events are Normal; no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy event appears.

The replacement ReplicaSet pod templates are identical to the previous ones except for the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt (ad-5f8dd7c58d 2026-11-16T14:39:27Z, payment-5d565cf9b 2026-11-16T14:39:26Z): same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-payment, same env lists, same resources (ad limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, payment limits cpu 20m / memory 160Mi). The outgoing ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 are scaled to 0 replicas.

The new ad container started at 14:39:29 but its application only became able to serve at 14:45:49: its log contains "Ad service starting." at 2026-11-16T14:44:09.972878021Z and "Ad service started, listening on 8080" at 2026-11-16T14:45:49.975023314Z, with the first ad-request log lines after that (e.g. "Non-targeted ad request received" at 14:47:59).

The new payment container started at 14:39:29 and emitted "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" only at 2026-11-16T14:40:51.46Z (the only payment log line in 14:39:00-14:41:00), after which it logged successful "Charge request received." / "Transaction complete." pairs, beginning 14:46:09 onwards in the inspected slice.

Neither the ad nor the payment Deployment defines a readinessProbe or livenessProbe (both null), and in the namespace only otel-collector has one (probe "yes"); ad's container limits are cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and payment's are cpu 20m / memory 160Mi, so a replacement pod is treated as ready the moment its container starts.

Each affected Service has exactly one backend address, so its pod's unavailability is a full backend outage: Endpoints ad resolves to pod ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 (100.96.1.149) on node i-068d8c8f254eed0b1 and Endpoints payment to pod payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn (100.96.1.157), with no other addresses.

checkout's client spans to payment failed in the same short burst: oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had 79.74 error spans in the 120s window ending 14:41:16 and 42.67 in the window ending 14:43:16, and 0 errors in every later window, with 54-113 successful (UNSET) spans per window throughout.

The new pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 (ad-5f8dd7c58d-rtbj5 created 14:39:27, payment-5d565cf9b-8gwcn created 14:39:26, both on node i-068d8c8f254eed0b1), and all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

Degradation did not persist to the end of the window: in 14:40:00-14:59:16 frontend's error spans were 417.17 on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and GET /api/data (plus its nested duplicates), 75.66 on the checkout path and 12.61 on tcp.connect, and the last sampled GetAds window (ending 14:53:16) shows 0 errors with 176.18 successful spans.

Primary causal chain: the ad Deployment's pod was replaced at 14:39:27-14:39:29 as a plain rollout restart (identical template apart from restartedAt); because the Deployment has no readiness probe and the ad Service has a single backend, the new pod was routed traffic while its Node.js process had not yet bound port 8080 (listening at 14:45:49.98), so frontend's GetAds calls failed (417.17 error spans in 14:40-14:59) and frontend returned errors on GET /api/data, producing the RequestErrorRate alert at 14:40:30.

Second, smaller contributor: the payment Deployment was restarted in the same operation (new ReplicaSet 14:39:26, pod started 14:39:29) and its gRPC server only started listening at 14:40:51.46 with no readiness probe, so checkout's Charge calls failed for ~2 minutes (79.74 + 42.67 error spans) and frontend's POST /api/checkout errored (75.66 error spans in 14:40-14:59). This is a separate object from ad and accounts for the minority of the frontend error spans.

Coordinated rollout restarts of single-replica dependencies without readiness gates are the mechanism, not a configuration change: the only difference between the retired and replacement ReplicaSets is the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt pod-template annotation, images and limits/memory are unchanged, the image was reported already present on the node at 14:39:29, and the pre-existing ad pod was built from the identical template.

Rejected: an image or configuration regression in ad/payment. The replacement ReplicaSets carry the same images (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, :2.1.3-payment), the same env arrays and the same resource limits as the retired ReplicaSets; the kubelet reported the image "already present on machine" at container creation, and the deployments' Available/Progressing conditions are True with NewReplicaSetAvailable.

Rejected: pod crash, OOMKill or eviction as the impact on ad/payment pods. Both surviving pods have restartCount 0, the only events involving them are Killing/SuccessfulDelete of the predecessors and Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/SuccessfulCreate of the replacements (all Normal), and no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy event appears.

Rejected: node-level resource pressure on i-068d8c8f254eed0b1 (which hosts ad, payment and 13 other otel-demo pods). All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False; apart from the two intentionally restarted pods, the listed otel-demo pods report restartCount 0.

Rejected: a flagd-side fault producing the GetAds failures. During the outage ad produced no GetAds server spans at all (0 in the windows ending 14:45:16-14:49:16), while ad's only error spans in the whole window are 1.02 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and 1.33 on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean, and recommendation's comparable flagd EventStream count is 4.07 - orders of magnitude below the 417 failed GetAds spans, so flagd does not explain the frontend error burst.

Checked and healthy: payment recorded 0 error spans in the window and logged successful "Charge request received."/"Transaction complete." pairs continuously after 14:40:51; accounting recorded 0 error spans; frontend's own spans to cart, product-catalog and recommendation carried no error status; and ad, checkout and frontend all resumed normal (error-free) span flow by the last sampled window ending 14:53:16, i.e. the failure was a transient startup gap, not a persistent defect in those callers.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alert rule is not loaded in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate and by type=alert both returned no_data (no rules), so the alert's exact expression and the meaning of its value 4.422222222222222 (rate unit, window, denominator) cannot be verified; no Alertmanager data source is available in this Run.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend: traces_search and traces_search_by_tags (error=true) both returned status no_data for 14:20-14:50, so the exact gRPC status codes and error messages on the failing GetAds/PlaceOrder spans are unknown; the failure mode (connection refused vs deadline exceeded) is inferred only from tcp.connect error spans and latency buckets.
frontend's container log view returned no_data (0 bytes, 0 lines read), so there is no application-side error text from the alerting service itself.

ad's error-filtered log view returned no_data (0 of 218 lines matched the error filter), so 'no error logged by ad' is a limit of what was read, not proof; ad's container was also reported to have no previous instance, so pre-restart ad logs are unavailable.

kube_pod_container_info has no series for namespace otel-demo in this Prometheus (both the instant query and get_series returned no_data), so image digests could not be compared between old and new pods; image identity rests on the ReplicaSet templates and the kubelet's "already present on machine" message.
The NetworkPolicy listing in otel-demo returned no_data, so network-level isolation as a factor remains unverified rather than excluded.

No change-history integration is available, so who or what issued the kubectl rollout restart of ad and payment at 14:39:26-14:39:27 (operator, pipeline, or fault injection) is unknown, as is the Deployment state before that moment beyond the retired ReplicaSet templates.

Why the ad container needed ~4 minutes before logging "Ad service starting." is not directly measurable: no container CPU-throttling or usage metrics are available in this target, so the 50m CPU limit is a plausible but unproven contributor to the long startup.

Other services' error series (cart, currency, email, shipping, product-catalog, quote, kafka, image-provider, load-generator) were not returned by the per-service error query; that is unknown rather than proven zero, although frontend's own spans to cart/product-catalog/recommendation showed no errors.
next_steps: Add readinessProbe (and a startupProbe with a generous failureThreshold) to the ad and payment Deployments, and audit the other otel-demo Deployments that lack probes (all except otel-collector), so a replacement pod is not added to Service endpoints before it listens on its port.
Review ad's CPU limit (50m) and consider raising it or setting a startup CPU burst, since the replacement ad container took ~4m40s before logging startup and ~6m20s to listen on 8080.

Treat restarting single-replica, probe-less dependencies as a change-controlled action (or run 2 replicas / maxUnavailable 0) so a rollout restart of ad or payment does not black out the frontend's /api/data and /api/checkout paths.
Verify the RequestErrorRate alert rule and its threshold in the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration that actually holds it, because the rule is absent from the Prometheus queried here.
